facts.statement: Pleistorallus flemingi is an extinct bird belonging to the rail family.
facts.quote: Pleistorallus flemingi, also referred to as Fleming's rail, is a genus and species of extinct bird in the rail family

facts.statement: This bird was a large and stout rail roughly the same size as the living takahē.
facts.quote: It was a large and stout rail about the same size as the extant takahē.

facts.statement: Trevor Worthy described the species in 1997 based on fossils found near Marton in New Zealand's North Island.
facts.quote: It was described by Trevor Worthy in 1997 from fossil material (a right tibiotarsus and distal left femur) found in coastal deposits near Marton, in the Rangitikei District of the North Island.

facts.statement: The animal lived in New Zealand during the Middle Pleistocene, approximately one million years ago.
facts.quote: from the Middle Pleistocene (about one million years ago) of New Zealand.

facts.statement: The genus Pleistorallus is classified within the family Rallidae.
Fossils of this genus date from the Gelasian to the Late Pleistocene, between 2.58 and 0.0117 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Gelasian to Late Pleistocene (2.58 to 0.0117 million years ago)
